_comment: Known-red entries: defects that are real, triaged, and not yet fixed.
Committed to the repo on purpose. `thalamus ceremony ack` keeps its store machine-local,
which would leave it empty in CI and make every known-red read there as a new regression.
`witness_contains` is the positive pin, and it is what stops this file being a mute button:
an entry that only says 'this fails' absorbs any future failure at the same site, while one
that names part of the witness breaks the moment the defect changes shape.
Delete an entry in the same change that fixes its defect. A stale entry makes the suite
exit 2, which is deliberate - a silently-fixed defect hides the next regression at that site.

expectations.witness_contains: close_window recorded 1 forced kill(s) ['close'] and kill-window ran=True
expectations.note: Issue #151. close_window polls #{pane_dead} and discards it, so a pane that exited gracefully under remain-on-exit is waited out for the whole grace budget and then force-killed and recorded as never distilled. The pin names both halves of the current behaviour - the forced-kill record AND the kill-window - so a partial repair that stopped one and not the other drifts rather than staying triaged.

expectations.witness_contains: '-t 0' (a chunk that retargets the send to a pane of its own choosing) -> pane held ''
expectations.note: Issue #152. Text posted to /api/send is read by tmux as arguments. The pin is the retarget payload rather than the dash-flag ones because it is the sharpest of the set: a repair that added `--` fixes every entry in the witness at once, and a repair that somehow left this one would drift here.

Issue #74. do_POST guards the JSON parse and nothing after it, so any body that parses to a non-object, and several wrong-typed fields, escape as unhandled exceptions and kill the handler thread. The count is the pin: it is a denominator over routes derived from the shipped dispatch, so fixing any route, or adding one, moves it and drifts.
